channel.title: BRYME — writing opportunities, guides and verification
channel.description: Legitimate paid-writing opportunities, practical guides and BRYME's firsthand verification record.

item.title: The Missouri Review
item.description: The Missouri Review pays $25 per printed page for poetry, fiction and nonfiction, and $100 per story or essay accepted for BLAST, its online exclusive

item.title: Menagerie: $50 per acceptance, no reprints, 60-90 day reply
item.description: Menagerie pays $50 per acceptance - one piece of prose or one to three poems - and acquires first serial rights.

item.title: The Maine Review
item.description: The Maine Review pays a $25 honorarium per published flash piece and per poem, and $50 for prose of 1,001 words or more; artwork is paid $50 on publication.

item.title: The Literary Fantasy Magazine
item.description: The Literary Fantasy Magazine pays a $10 token payment for fiction accepted for Arcanist Online, its web publication, and says its print magazines pay more.

item.title: Invisible City: $20 per piece, open now
item.description: Invisible City pays a $20 honorarium for every published piece, with international contributors paid by wire transfer.

item.title: InterrobangLit: $3 token payment per accepted story
item.description: InterrobangLit pays a $3 token payment by PayPal for each accepted prose piece, and its submission windows are free.

item.title: Ink In Thirds: $5 per contributor, free to submit, no AI
item.description: Ink In Thirds pays $5 per contributor, with a floor of $3 should donations fall, and charges no fees.

item.title: Infrarrealista Review
item.description: Infrarrealista Review pays $100 per book review or cultural-criticism essay and $50 per interview, and pays $50 a publication for poems and short fiction in

item.title: The Idaho Review: $300 a story, $75 a poem, no entry fee
item.description: The Idaho Review pays $300 for a short story and $75 for each accepted poem, sends two copies of the print issue, and charges no entry fee.

item.title: HEART: $25 on publication for poems and short prose
item.description: HEART pays $25 on publication, whether the work appears on the site or in the digital issue, and runs a separate annual HEART Poetry Award of $500.

item.title: Half Mystic Journal
item.description: Half Mystic Journal pays US$20 for each piece it accepts into its Fioritura issue, with submissions closing in April 2027.

item.title: Gavialidae: $150 per poem or flash, $500 per story or essay
item.description: Gavialidae pays $150 per poem or flash fiction piece and $500 per short story or essay, reading unpublished work year-round through Duosuma.

item.title: Frontier Poetry: $50 per poem on the free New Voices route
item.description: Frontier Poetry pays $50 for every poem selected on its New Voices route, which is always open and always free to enter, for poets with no more than one

item.title: F(r)iction: $25 per printed page, $2.50 to submit, no AI
item.description: F(r)iction pays $25 per final printed page and sends two free contributor copies, with a $2.50 charge per submission that the magazine says goes toward paying

item.title: Free the Verse: $10 a poem, $20 for Marginalia
item.description: Free the Verse pays $10 for a poem in its themed quarterly issue and $20 for a Marginalia piece that annotates a poem's first and final drafts.

item.title: The First Line: $25-$50 fiction, $10-$25 other
item.description: The First Line pays $10 for a poem, $25 for a nonfiction essay and $25 to $50 for a story, plus a copy of the issue, and states flatly that it will never

item.title: Fairy Tale Review
item.description: Fairy Tale Review pays a $50 honorarium and sends two copies of the issue to each contributor.

item.title: The Fairy Tale Magazine: $25 USD per published poem or story
item.description: The Fairy Tale Magazine pays $25 USD for each poem and prose piece it publishes, and its fall call is free to enter.

item.title: Fahmidan Journal: $35 per piece, four reading windows a year
item.description: Fahmidan Journal pays $35 for every piece it publishes, delivered on publication, and has paid that since Issue 24 in September 2025.

item.title: Consequence: $20-$150, paying print
item.description: Consequence pays for everything it prints: $20 a poem, $30-$50 a prose piece by length, $150 for an eight-page art spread in print, $50 online and $30 on

item.title: Colorado Review: $300 for stories and essays, $100 for poems
item.description: Colorado Review pays $300 for short stories and nonfiction, a flat $100 to each poet featured, and $100 for cover photography.

item.title: Claudine: $25 per micro, 400 words max, free and no AI
item.description: Claudine pays $25 on publication for microfiction and micro creative nonfiction of up to 400 words, and submissions are always free.

item.title: Chicago Review of Books: $25 for reviews, $75 for features
item.description: The Chicago Review of Books pays $25 for reviews and interviews and $75 for features, taking pitches by email two to three months ahead of a book's

item.title: Booth: $50 for every published piece, open 1 September
item.description: Booth pays $50 for every piece it publishes, whatever the length, sent by PayPal after online publication.

item.title: Blue Marble Review
item.description: Blue Marble Review pays $30 for each piece published online and $75 for cover art, and is open to students aged 13 to 22 - an age limit, not a country one.

item.title: Blackbird: $40 per poem, $200 per story or essay
item.description: Blackbird pays $40 per poem, $200 per story or essay, and $100 for book reviews, craft essays and interviews.

item.title: Black Warrior Review
item.description: Black Warrior Review states plainly that it pays contributors, and equally plainly that the amount depends on how many contributors an issue carries and the

item.title: Berkeley Fiction Review
item.description: Berkeley Fiction Review pays $25 for each accepted story and sends a complimentary copy of the issue, and states that it does not charge submission fees.

item.title: Bennington Review
item.description: Bennington Review pays $120 for prose up to six typeset pages and $250 beyond that, plus $25 per poem, along with copies of the issue.

item.title: Bayou Magazine: $150 or $100 per story by length
item.description: Bayou Magazine pays $150 for fiction of 3,000 words or more and $100 for shorter stories, and pays other genres in contributor copies.
